::: {.hero}
# biblioflow

`biblioflow` is a planned Python-native toolkit for bibliographic metadata,
bibliometrics, science mapping, and literature-review data workflows. It is
inspired by the R bibliometrics ecosystem, especially `bibliometrix`, while
using Pythonic naming and dataframe-centric workflows.

This repository is currently a scaffold. Core implementation will be added in
later changes.
:::

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Bibliographic ingestion

Planned ingestion support includes RIS, BibTeX, Scopus CSV, Web of Science
exports, PubMed NBIB/XML, PubMed Central XML, OpenAlex, Crossref, Lens,
Dimensions, Cochrane, and generic formats.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Canonical metadata

Normalize provider-specific records into a canonical dataset while preserving
raw records for traceability.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Bibliometric analysis

Compute descriptive indicators, matrices, networks, thematic maps, thematic
evolution, conceptual structures, and historiographs.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Pythonic API

Use a compact API such as `load()`, `analyze()`, `matrix()`, `network()`,
`map_themes()`, `trace_themes()`, and `export()`.
:::
:::

## Intended minimal example

```python
import biblioflow as bf

records = bf.load("data/scopus_export.bib", provider="scopus")
summary = bf.analyze(records)
network = bf.network(records, kind="co_occurrence", unit="keywords_all")
```

## Naming policy

The project name is `biblioflow` for the PyPI package, Python import package,
and planned command-line interface. Do not use a hyphenated alias.
